name: Guinea
summary: The first French African colony to reject France’s offer of continued ties (1958); later ruled by Sékou Touré and military governments; rich in bauxite.

location.value: West Africa on the Atlantic; 245,857 km² (2025 census).

climate.value: Tropical, with a long, heavy rainy season on the coast and a drier climate in the north.

resources.value: Bauxite (among the world’s largest reserves), iron ore, gold and diamonds.

disasters.value: Floods and landslides in Conakry in the rainy season.

urbanisation.value: Conakry, the capital, is a crowded port city on a peninsula.

disease.value: The Ebola epidemic of 2014–16 began in Guinea and killed over 11,000 people in West Africa.

migration.value: Refugees came from the wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone in the 1990s–2000s.

economicBase.value: Bauxite: 25% or more of the world’s known reserves; the second-largest producer.

tradeRoutes.value: Bauxite is shipped from Boké and Conakry to Europe, China and the Gulf.

wealth.value: HDI 0.500 (rated low, 181st, 2023). The article does not state a low-income classification.

moneyAndTax.value: The Guinean franc, reintroduced in 1985 after the failed syli of the 1970s.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A republic, governed since the 2021 coup as a de facto military autocracy.

keyRulers.value: Ahmed Sékou Touré (from independence until his death on 26 March 1984). Lansana Conté (1984–2008). Later and present leaders are not named here.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Guinea (checked 12 Nov 2026); Britannica Kids: Sékou Touré (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Touré led Guinea from independence until he died on 26 March 1984; about a week later a military coup overthrew his regime)

succession.value: Moussa Dadis Camara seized control after Conté’s death on 23 December 2008. The coup of 5 September 2021 was led by Mamady Doumbouya.

institutions.value: Weak institutions, frequent coups and states of emergency.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The army has played a major role in politics, ruling in 1984–2010 and 2021 onward.

majorWars.value: Spillover from wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone.

territoryChange.value: The borders drawn by France have stayed the same since independence.

alliancesRivals.value: Close to the Soviet bloc in the 1960s after the break with France; a member of ECOWAS, which suspended it after the 2021 coup.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Literacy is low, though education has grown since the 1980s.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Roads and mining railways carry bauxite and iron ore to the coast.

religion.value: Sources differ: 89.1% Muslim and 6.8% Christian in the infobox (2022), 86.8% Muslim, 3.52% Christian and 9.42% animist in the body text (ARDA, 2023).

languageWriting.value: French is official; Fula, Mandinka, Susu and other languages are widely spoken.

artsArchitecture.value: Music and dance traditions, including the national band Bembeya Jazz and the djembe drum.

dailyLife.value: Many families farm rice and cassava, and rice with sauce is the staple dish.

neighbours.value: Senegal, Mali, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea-Bissau.

ideasReligions.value: African socialism under the first president, Sékou Touré (ruled 1958–84), who also suppressed opponents.

colonisation.value: A French colony (part of French West Africa) until 1958.

riseSignals.value: Voted overwhelmingly for independence in the referendum of 28 September 1958; independence proclaimed on 2 October 1958.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Guinea (checked 12 Nov 2026); Britannica Kids: Sékou Touré (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Guinea became the first independent French-speaking African state on 2 October 1958; the 28 September referendum is not on this page)

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Guinea continues as an independent state.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
